Summary

Adds first-class self-hosting support for OSIRIS without touching any
application logic — only deployment files, an icon, and docs.

- **`.dockerignore`** — excludes `node_modules`, `.next`, `.git` and the large
  `*.diff` artifacts from the build context (faster, slimmer image).
- **`docker-compose.yml`**
  - `image:` (`ghcr.io/simplifaisoul/osiris:latest`) + `build:` fallback —
    pulls the published image when available, otherwise builds from the local
    `Dockerfile`.
  - **configurable host port** via `${OSIRIS_PORT:-3000}` (default `3000`) —
    remap without editing the file by setting `OSIRIS_PORT` in `.env`.
  - optional `env_file: .env` (`required: false`).
  - full **CasaOS `x-casaos:`** metadata (title, description, icon, port map,
    per-env descriptions). Plain Docker Compose ignores it; CasaOS reads it.
- **`public/casaos-icon.png`** — 512×512 PNG of the gold Eye-of-Horus mark,
  used as the CasaOS app icon. Ships in this PR, so the `icon:` URL resolves
  once merged.
- **`.env.template`** — documents every supported variable, incl. `OSIRIS_PORT`.
- **`DOCKER.md`** — complete self-hosting guide (Compose, `docker run`, GHCR
  pull, CasaOS install, image internals, API keys).
- **`README.md`** — new Docker/Self-Hosting section with GHCR pull + custom
  port notes; replaces the outdated `OPENSKY_USERNAME`/`OPENSKY_PASSWORD` block
  (OpenSky moved to OAuth2 in March 2025).

All image/icon references use this project's own namespace
(`ghcr.io/simplifaisoul`, `raw.githubusercontent.com/simplifaisoul`) so nothing
points at a contributor's account.

## API keys — what's actually wired up

While documenting this I audited the routes: the only env vars the current code
reads are **`SCANNER_URL`** and **`SCANNER_KEY`** (the RECON scanner backend).
Every other feed is keyless (aviation → `adsb.lol`, satellites →
`celestrak.org`, fires → NASA FIRMS open CSV, quakes → USGS, etc.).

`FIRMS_API_KEY`, `OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `N2YO_API_KEY` and `AIS_API_KEY`
are documented as **optional / reserved** (signup links + rate limits in
`DOCKER.md`) since they appear in the env example but aren't consumed yet —
handy if/when those routes are upgraded to authenticated sources.

## How the Docker Compose works

`docker compose up -d` runs the multi-stage `node:22-alpine` standalone image
(~220 MB, non-root `nextjs` uid 1001), serves `node server.js` on container
port 3000 published as `OSIRIS_PORT` (default 3000), auto-loads `.env` if
present, and restarts unless stopped.

## Testing

- `docker build` → image builds clean (220 MB).
- Container starts: `▲ Next.js 16.2.6 … Ready`; `GET /` returns **HTTP 200**.
- `docker compose config` validates; verified running with a remapped
  `OSIRIS_PORT` and installed as a managed app via
  `casaos-cli app-management install`.

## For maintainers

To enable the prebuilt-image path, publish `ghcr.io/simplifaisoul/osiris`
(e.g. via a release workflow). Until then the `build:` fallback builds locally,
so the compose works as-is.
